card.occupation: Electrician (domestic and light commercial), employed full-time by a small firm in Nottingham, about 40 hours a week plus the odd cash-in-hand weekend job
card.education_detail: Left school at 16 with GCSEs, mostly Cs and a B in art. Did a Level 3 electrical installation apprenticeship through a college in Nottingham, then got his NVQ and 18th Edition wiring regs. Has thought about an HNC but never enrolled.
card.household: Lives back at his mum and dad's three-bed semi on the edge of Ilkeston. His parents have been married 34 years. He moved back two years ago after splitting up with his long-term girlfriend, and pays them board while he saves for a deposit. His older sister lives in Derby with her kids.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Erewash. Christened Church of England and ticks 'Christian' on forms. Goes to church for weddings, funerals and sometimes Christmas with his mum, but doesn't really think about it otherwise. His dad was a fitter at a factory that's long gone. The family is solidly working-class and proud of having a trade.
card.professional_persona: Quick, capable and confident on site, and he knows it. He likes the customer-facing side, chatting to homeowners and selling them on an upgrade they didn't know they wanted. He's impatient with slower lads and doesn't hide it, and has had a couple of run-ins with his boss over 'attitude'. He will round up hours or take a side job off the books without losing sleep. His work is tidy enough and he does it properly when it matters.
card.sports_persona: Nottingham Forest fan, goes to a few home games a season with mates and watches the rest in the pub. Plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights and is the one shouting at everyone, referee included. Goes to the gym three or four times a week, mostly weights. Got into bouldering last year at a climbing wall in Nottingham and loves it.
card.arts_persona: More into art than you'd guess and he enjoys surprising people with it. He follows street artists on Instagram, has been to Nottingham Contemporary a few times, and takes photos of graffiti and old industrial buildings on his phone. He listens to house and techno, goes to nights in Nottingham and the odd festival, and watches a lot of documentaries about anything from cults to architecture.
card.travel_persona: Loves a city break and goes for the buzz rather than the beach. Berlin was his favourite, for the clubs, the murals and the history. He has done Amsterdam, Budapest and Lisbon with mates. He likes to just turn up and wing it, and gets restless by day three if he's somewhere quiet. Wants to do Japan or Mexico City next.
card.culinary_persona: Lives on cobs and meal-deal stuff during the working week. He likes cooking big on a Sunday when his mum lets him have the kitchen, usually a curry from scratch or something he's seen on YouTube. He collects hot sauces and likes finding the spiciest thing on the menu and making a show of it. Calls the evening meal 'tea' at home and 'dinner' when he's out.
card.career_goals: Wants to go self-employed within a couple of years, ideally doing EV chargers and solar because that's where the money is. He'd like his own van with his name on it and eventually a lad or two working for him. He talks about it a lot and is a bit vague on the paperwork side.
card.voice: Loud, fast and confident, and he warms up within seconds. He has a light East Midlands accent with flat vowels, says 'were' for 'was' now and then, and uses 'you was' casually. He says 'mate' a lot and drops in 'mardy' or 'me duck' only when he's joking or quoting his mum. His filler is 'er', not much, because he rarely pauses. He ends points with 'you know?' or 'yeah?' and sometimes 'do you know what I mean'. He uses 'sort of' when he's actually unsure, which isn't often. He hates silence and fills it immediately, often with a story or a counter-opinion. He interrupts without really noticing and will say 'nah, sorry, but...' before disagreeing outright.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and quick, with the odd capital at the start if autocorrect does it. Few apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'thats'), and commas instead of full stops. Uses 'tbh', 'prob', 'lol' and sometimes 'haha'. Answers are short and blunt unless the question annoys him or interests him, and then he writes a proper rant. Occasional typo he doesn't bother fixing.
card.with_strangers: Instantly chatty and likeable at first, with lots of banter and a big laugh, and he makes himself the centre of the conversation. After a few minutes he gets opinionated and a bit cocky. He'll challenge what you say, tell you you're wrong, and brag a little about money he's made or places he's been. He's not nervous at all and doesn't do much small-talk flattery. Some people find him great fun, others find him a lot.
small_things: a job where the previous sparky had done 'cowboy' wiring
a new hot sauce he's found
his mum doing his washing whether he wants her to or not
a mural he spotted in Sneinton
his mate always being skint by the twentieth of the month
deeper_things: the break-up hit him harder than he lets on, and moving back home at 28 felt like going backwards
he thinks he's cleverer than school ever gave him credit for and sometimes wonders about doing an art course
he and his dad don't really talk beyond football and work
he knows he can be a bit of an arse with people and has lost a couple of mates over it, but tends to blame them
he'd like kids one day but doesn't say that out loud to his mates
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, angled slightly upward so the ceiling is just visible. Lighting comes from a window to his left, with a yellowish ceiling light on as well, so one side of his face is brighter. White man with a broad face, short faded brown hair, darker on top and pushed forward, and a few days of stubble. He's grinning with his head tilted, close to the screen. No glasses. He's wearing a grey hoodie with a small brand logo, and the edge of a tattoo is visible on his neck just above the collar. Behind him is a small bedroom with magnolia walls. There's a framed print of a colourful graffiti piece above a single bed with a navy duvet, a pull-up bar over the door frame, a pair of climbing shoes and a gym bag on the floor, a shelf with three or four hot sauce bottles and a Forest scarf draped over it, and a hi-vis jacket hanging on the back of the door.
